statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42768 ("Multi-RecipientInfo Bleichenbacher Oracle in CMS_decrypt() and PKCS7_decrypt()", Low): CMS_decrypt() and PKCS7_decrypt() can act as a Bleichenbacher-style RSA decryption oracle when an attacker can supply CMS or S/MIME messages with several recipient infos and observe the error code or the decryption output. OpenSSL fixed it in 3.5.7 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt; fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/bbb151a83041705d9d001ed2f9c12f5523e1b54d, committed after OpenSSL 3.5.6). Alpine lists it fixed in openssl 3.5.7-r0 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-42768). The advisory states that the FIPS modules in OpenSSL 4.0, 3.6, 3.5 and 3.4 are not affected, as CMS and S/MIME processing happens outside the FIPS module boundary; the openssl-fips package ships the FIPS provider of the same OpenSSL 3.5 release. The DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl packages (origin openssl: libcrypto3, libssl3, openssl and its -dbg, -dev, -doc, -libs-static and -misc packages in the DHI Alpine repository, and openssl-fips in the DHI security repository) are published as 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2 (openssl-fips from 3.5.5_git20260330-r1 on), each for x86_64 and aarch64. The OpenSSL version string in libcrypto.so.3 (libcrypto3) and in fips.so (openssl-fips) of every build, read from packages verified against the index checksums, is the OpenSSL release in the package version. Every build before 3.5.7-r0, including 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, whose libcrypto reports OpenSSL 3.5.5, is based on OpenSSL 3.5.6 or older without the fix, and 3.5.7-r0 and every later build are based on OpenSSL 3.5.7 or later.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42768 ("Multi-RecipientInfo Bleichenbacher Oracle in CMS_decrypt() and PKCS7_decrypt()", Low): CMS_decrypt() and PKCS7_decrypt() can act as a Bleichenbacher-style RSA decryption oracle when an attacker can supply CMS or S/MIME messages with several recipient infos and observe the error code or the decryption output. OpenSSL fixed it in 3.5.7 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt; fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/bbb151a83041705d9d001ed2f9c12f5523e1b54d, committed after OpenSSL 3.5.6), which stops CMS and PKCS#7 decryption from disabling RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 implicit rejection, so the protection relies on the RSA implementation that performs the decryption supporting implicit rejection. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42768. The advisory states that the FIPS modules in OpenSSL 4.0, 3.6, 3.5 and 3.4 are not affected, and that OpenSSL 3.0, which does not implement RSA implicit rejection, remains exposed to variants of the Bleichenbacher/Marvin attack. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI security repository (the FIPS builds and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build only in the security repository). The Debian changelog shipped in libssl3t64 was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64 (25 versions, packages verified against the index checksums). No build of Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-42768; the first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 entry naming it. The openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the same OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds. In libcrypto.so.3 of the rebuilds of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u1 and 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, non-FIPS and FIPS, on amd64 and arm64, the debug symbols in libssl3t64-dbgsym show pkcs7_decrypt_rinfo and CMS_RecipientInfo_decrypt shrinking at the 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 rebuild, matching the removed calls. The FIPS builds' openssl.cnf (in the openssl package) sets default_properties = fips=yes, so RSA decryption is performed by the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider. OpenSSL added RSA implicit rejection in 3.2: the 3.1.2 RSA decryption code (providers/implementations/asymciphers/rsa_enc.c at openssl-3.1.2) has none, and the 3.1.2 fips.so of the FIPS builds of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 lacks the implicit-rejection parameter that the 3.5 fips.so of the matching non-FIPS builds carries (both architectures). The fix therefore has no effect in the FIPS builds, and every FIPS build is affected, while the non-FIPS builds of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and later are fixed. Each FIPS build sorts directly above the non-FIPS builds of the same Debian release, so the range reopens at the FIPS build of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 and closes again at the next non-FIPS release. The status is AFFECTED because the newest FIPS build is still affected.
